title: Fantasy Player News
description: Breaking Fantasy Football player news along with the impact for fantasy managers

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Alec Pierce (heel) good to go for Sunday
items.desc: Alec Pierce (heel) will be good to go for Sunday night's game against the Kansas City Chiefs.
items.impact: Pierce missed Indianapolis' practice on Thursday, but it looks like that was just for injury maintenance, as he was back and a full participant for them at practice on Friday. He carries no injury designation heading into the weekend and will play on Sunday night, although it remains quite possible that he will continue to have minor limitations while the team ramps his workload back up.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Anthony Richardson Sr. (groin) active for Week 2
items.desc: Anthony Richardson Sr. (groin) will be active for Sunday night's game against the Kansas City Chiefs.
items.impact: Richardson is going to be active for the Colts on Sunday night, so his groin injury is likely considered nothing more than a minor issue at this point. He will continue to serve as the QB2 for this team behind Daniel Jones.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Cooper DeJean (calf/abdomen) set to play Sunday
items.desc: Cooper DeJean (calf/abdomen) is set to play in Sunday's game against the Tennessee Titans.
items.impact: Neither of DeJean's injuries are serious at this point and he goes into the weekend without an injury designation. He will continue to play a big role on Philadelphia's defense moving forward, assuming he suffers no setbacks with his recovery.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jonathan Greenard (pec) won't play Sunday
items.desc: Jonathan Greenard (pec) won't play play in Sunday's game against the Tennessee Titans.
items.impact: The veteran edge rusher is going to be out this week, despite taking part at practice all week. He should return to the lineup and provide a nice boost to Philly's pass rush sometime in the near future.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jalen Carter (wrist) available to play Sunday
items.desc: Jalen Carter (wrist) will be available to play in Sunday's game against the Tennessee Titans.
items.impact: Philadelphia's defense gets some good news ahead of Sunday's game, with Carter receiving full clearance to play against the Titans. He should continue to be a game-wrecker in what projects to be an easy matchup against Tennessee's low-powered offense.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Daron Payne (knee) cleared to play Sunday
items.desc: Daron Payne (knee) has been cleared to play in Sunday's game against the Dallas Cowboys.
items.impact: Payne now has full clearance to play in Sunday's game against the Cowboys, which was to be expected after he was upgraded to a full participant at practice on Thursday. Look for his presence to make a positive impact on Washington's defensive front in this matchup and beyond.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Ladd McConkey (ribs) questionable for Sunday
items.desc: Ladd McConkey (ribs) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Raiders due to a rib injury.
items.impact: McConkey was a DNP Wednesday and Thursday but got back on the practice field Friday. His chances to play are more on the slim side, but if he plays, you need to start him against this Raiders defense. If he sits, Quentin Johnston and Tre Harris are next in line for targets.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Javon Kinlaw (back) officially questionable for Sunday
items.desc: Javon Kinlaw (back) is officially questionable for Sunday's game against the Cowboys.
items.impact: Kinlaw returned to practice on Friday and will officially be questionable to play in Washington's matchup against Dallas on Sunday. Their defensive front will be a little short on depth if he is ruled out ahead of kickoff for this game.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Odafe Oweh (calf) available to play Sunday
items.desc: Odafe Oweh (calf) will be available to play in Sunday's game against the Dallas Cowboys.
items.impact: As expected, Oweh is going to be available to play through his minor calf injury on Sunday. The team will need him to step up and help anchor down the defensive front in what projects to be a tough matchup against the Cowboys.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jaylin Lane (groin) good to go for Sunday
items.desc: Jaylin Lane (groin) is good to go for Sunday's game against the Dallas Cowboys.
items.impact: A groin injury left Lane limited at practice all week, but it's not a serious issue and won't affect his availability for Sunday's game against Dallas. He doesn't project to be fantasy relevant for the foreseeable future, however.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: K'Lavon Chaisson (knee) off injury report for Sunday
items.desc: K'Lavon Chaisson (knee) is off of the injury report for Sunday's game against the Dallas Cowboys.
items.impact: Chaisson will be available to play on Sunday after managing a knee issue at practice throughout the week. He will continue to play an important role for the Commanders in their divisional matchup against Dallas' talented offense.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Greg Newsome II (rib) again limited on Friday
items.desc: Greg Newsome II (rib) was again a limited participant at practice on Friday.
items.impact: Newsome was limited for a second-straight practice on Friday as he continues to battle a rib injury of some kind. Deonte Banks (calf) and Paulson Adebo (Knee/IR) are both injured members of New York's secondary as well, so they may be much thinner than usual in Monday night's tough matchup against the Rams.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Deonte Banks (calf) downgraded to non-participant Friday
items.desc: Deonte Banks (calf) was downgraded to a non-participant at practice on Friday.
items.impact: Banks was not able to practice on Friday after being limited by a calf injury on Thursday. It looks like he's trending the wrong way for Week 2, which is bad news for the Giants, considering that they are dealing with multiple key injuries in their secondary.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Andrew Thomas (ankle) limited again Friday
items.desc: Andrew Thomas (ankle) was limited at practice again on Friday.
items.impact: The star offensive lineman has been limited at two-straight practices to start the week. It looks like he's trending towards playing on Monday night, assuming he suffers no setbacks between now and then.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: B.J. Hill (Achilles) questionable for Sunday
items.desc: B.J. Hill (Achilles) is questionable for the Bengals game against the Texans on Sunday.
items.impact: Hill was not in uniform during the teams practice, so it's unlikely he plays this weekend. He'll have to wait another week to see the field.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Cedric Gray (concussion) officially questionable for Sunday
items.desc: Cedric Gray (concussion) is officially questionable for Sunday's game against the Philadelphia eagles.
items.impact: Gray has been a full participant at practice all week but still has yet to officially the NFL's concussion protocols, so he will be questionable to play in Week 2. His absence would be bad news for Tennessee's defense in a matchup against the Eagles this week.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Joe Burrow (back) questionable for Sunday
items.desc: Joe Burrow (back) is questionable for the Bengals game against the Texans due to a back injury. Burrow has told the media he would play.
items.impact: The questionable tag is likely a formality given Burrows limited practice status throughout the week. He should be fine and good to go against a Texans defense that just got bulldozed by the Bills.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Sean Tucker (hamstring) available to play for Sunday
items.desc: Sean Tucker (hamstring) will be available to play in Sunday's game against the Cleveland Browns.
items.impact: As expected, Tucker is back near full health and is going to be available to play against the Browns on Sunday. He is expected to be squarely behind Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell in the team's pecking order, however, making him irrelevant for fantasy purposes.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jalen McMillan (knee) questionable for Sunday
items.desc: Jalen McMillan (knee) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Cleveland Browns.
items.impact: McMillan was able to practice in a full capacity all week, but he still hasn't received full clearance to play and is officially questionable heading into the weekend. If he's unable to suit up this week, look for rookie Ted Hurst III to see more work as a result of his absence.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jerry Jeudy (wrist) good to go for Sunday
items.desc: Jerry Jeudy (wrist) is good to go for Sunday's game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
items.impact: Jeudy is going to be good to go on Sunday, which was expected after he was able to practice without limitations this week. He isn't expected to be a relevant fantasy option for however long Deshaun Watson is starting for the Browns, however.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Elgton Jenkins (back) cleared to play for Sunday
items.desc: Elgton Jenkins (back) has been cleared to play in Sunday's game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
items.impact: Jenkins will be available to play on Sunday despite being on the injury report recently due to a back injury. Tevin Jenkins (back) has been ruled out for Cleveland, however, so their offensive line will still be at less than full power against the Buccaneers.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Nico Collins (hamstring) ruled out for Sunday
items.desc: Nico Collins (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Cincinnati Bengals.
items.impact: Collins recently suffered a hamstring injury and will not be able to play in Sunday's game as a result. It may cause him to miss more time beyond this game as well, but we likely won't know more about his official recovery timeline until later this week or next. Look for Dalton Schultz, Kayshon Boutte, and Jaylin Noel to see more work as a result of his absence against the Bengals in Week 2.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Darnell Washington (personal) set to play Sunday
items.desc: Darnell Washington (personal) is set to play in Sunday's game against the New England Patriots.
items.impact: Washington missed two practices while tending to a personal issue earlier in the week, but he carries no designation heading into the weekend and will be available to play against the Patriots. He doesn't project to have fantasy relevance for the foreseeable future, however.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Troy Fautanu (ankle) listed questionable for Sunday
items.desc: Troy Fautanu (ankle) is listed questionable for Sunday's game against the New England Patriots.
items.impact: The Steelers are at risk of playing without their starting left tackle on Sunday, as Fautanu is currently questionable to play due to an ankle injury. His absence would be a big hit to Pittsburgh's offense in an already-tough road matchup in Week 2.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Joey Porter Jr. (conditioning/back) won't play Sunday
items.desc: Joey Porter Jr. (conditioning/back) won't play in Sunday's game against the New England Patriots.
items.impact: Porter will be out for another game on Sunday. He's still ramping up his conditioning, and the team doesn't feel confident that he is ready to retake the field at this point. His absence will make life easier for Drake Maye and New England's offense on the other side of the ball.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) questionable to play Sunday
items.desc: Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) is questionable to play in Sunday's game against the New England Patriots.
items.impact: Pittman recently suffered a foot injury and missed Pittsburgh's final two practices of the week because of it. He will still have a chance to play in Week 2, as he officially carries a questionable tag ahead of their matchup against the Patriots. DK Metcalf and Pat Freiermuth will both see an increase in work if the veteran is ruled out for that matchup.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Carlton Davis III (neck) officially questionable for Sunday
items.desc: Carlton Davis III (neck) is officially questionable for Sunday's game against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
items.impact: As expected, Davis is officially listed with a questionable tag heading into the weekend. He seems to have an uphill battle at playing on Sunday, however, as he wasn't able to take part in any of the team's practices this week, even in a limited fashion.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Dre'Mont Jones (foot) questionable for Sunday
items.desc: Dre'Mont Jones (foot) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
items.impact: The veteran edge rusher is at risk of missing Sunday's game due to a foot injury that left him limited at practice all week. It looks like he's trending towards playing through it, however, which will be much needed for a New England defense that already lacks talent at edge rusher.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) officially good to go for Sunday
items.desc: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is off of the injury report and officially good to go for Sunday's game against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
items.impact: New England's offense is set to get a much-needed boost this week with their young running back off of the injury report and set to make his season debut on Sunday. Henderson projects to be something of a 'boom-or-bust' fantasy option on a week-to-week basis while he continues to split work with Rhamondre Stevenson in the Patriots' backfield.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Paulson Adebo (knee) placed on injured reserve
items.desc: Paulson Adebo (knee) has been placed on injured reserve and will be out for at least four weeks.
items.impact: The veteran cornerback lands on injured reserve after suffering a knee injury, which means that he will be sidelined for at least four weeks while he recovers. New York is dealing with multiple injuries to key players in their secondary right now, so their defense could take a big hit if those continue to stack up over the next couple of weeks.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: John Simpson (groin) questionable for Sunday
items.desc: John Simpson (groin) is questionable for Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints.
items.impact: Simpson's groin injury will leave him with a questionable tag ahead of Sunday's game against the Saints. Ronnie Stanley (toe) is also questionable to play in that matchup, so Baltimore's offensive line may look weaker than usual if one or both of those guys are unable to suit up.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Devontez Walker (groin) good to go for Sunday
items.desc: Devontez Walker (groin) will be good to go for Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints.
items.impact: To no surprise, Walker has received full clearance to play on Sunday after practicing without limitations all week. He is primed to see more work than usual with Zay Flowers (hamstring) doubtful to play for the Ravens in Week 2.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Teddye Buchanan (knee) won't play Sunday
items.desc: Teddye Buchanan (knee) won't play in Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints.
items.impact: The Ravens will be without Buchanan on Sunday. They are dealing with several key injuries on the defensive side of the ball and will be thinner than usual in what projects to be a tough matchup against New Orleans' effective offense.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Trey Hendrickson (finger) listed questionable for Sunday
items.desc: Trey Hendrickson (finger) is listed as questionable to play in Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints.
items.impact: The Ravens may be without their star edge rusher on Sunday, as he's currently considered questionable to play due to a finger injury. Nnamdi Madubuike (neck) has already been ruled out for Baltimore, so their defensive front is already set to be weaker than usual in a matchup against New Orleans' potent offense in Week 2.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Nnamdi Madubuike (neck) unavailable for Sunday
items.desc: Nnamdi Madubuike (neck) will be unavailable for Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints.
items.impact: Madubuike was able to practice in a limited fashion all week, but the team still doesn't think he's quite ready to make his season debut and has ruled him out for Sunday's game. Baltimore's defensive front will be operating at less than full strength without him and will be especially weak if Trey Hendrickson (finger) is also ruled out.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Ronnie Stanley (toe) officially questionable for Sunday
items.desc: Ronnie Stanley (toe) is officially questionable for Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints.
items.impact: Stanley was able to return to practice on Friday after being absent earlier in the week due to a toe injury. He is questionable and will have a chance to play on Sunday, but we won't know his status with certainty until sometime closer to kickoff.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Zay Flowers (hamstring) doubtful to play Sunday
items.desc: Zay Flowers (hamstring) is doubtful to play in Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints.
items.impact: Flowers is officially going into the weekend with a doubtful tag, meaning that he is almost certainly going to be sidelined against the Saints thanks to the hamstring injury that he suffered in Week 1. It remains to be seen if he will have to miss more time beyond this game, and fantasy managers should look for Rashod Bateman and Devontez Walker to benefit from his absence and see more work on Sunday.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Darnell Wright (knee) cleared to play Sunday
items.desc: Darnell Wright (knee) has been cleared to play in Sunday's game against the Minnesota Vikings.
items.impact: There was some concern for Wright's health earlier in the week when he missed practice due to a knee issue, but it turned out to be nothing more than a minor issue and he has received full clearance to play through it against the Vikings. That's good news for Chicago's offense as a whole as they look to build off of the great success they found in the season opener last week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Kyle Monangai (hamstring) off injury report for Sunday
items.desc: Kyle Monangai (hamstring) is off of the injury report ahead of Sunday's matchup against the Minnesota Vikings.
items.impact: Monangai is going to be good to go for Sunday's game, despite being limited at practice earlier in the week due to a hamstring injury. He shouldn't have any limitations and will likely continue to be an involved backup behind D'Andre Swift in this game and beyond.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: D'Andre Swift (ankle/knee) good to go for Sunday
items.desc: D'Andre Swift (ankle/knee) is good to go for Sunday's game against the Minnesota Vikings.
items.impact: Swift was limited at practice earlier in the week due to a couple of injuries that he was dealing with, but neither of them are serious and he carries no injury designation heading into the weekend. Kyle Monangai (hamstring) is also good to go, so Chicago's backfield should continue operating as usual in a divisional matchup against the Vikings on Sunday.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Brock Bowers (knee) doubtful to play Sunday
items.desc: Brock Bowers (knee) is doubtful to play in Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Chargers.
items.impact: HC Klint Kubiak told reporters that Bowers is doubtful to play on Sunday, despite making his return to the practice field on Friday. It looks like he's trending the right way for Week 3, but fantasy managers will have to wait at least another week for him and should expect Michael Mayer to see more opportunities in the meantime.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: J.J. McCarthy to serve as QB2 on Sunday
items.desc: J.J. McCarthy will serve as Minnesota's backup quarterback against the Chicago Bears on Sunday.
items.impact: The young quarterback has moved a slot up on the depth chart for Week 2 with Kyler Murray (concussion) being ruled out for Minnesota's matchup against the Bears. He isn't likely to see the field with Carson Wentz set to start, but if anything happens to the veteran, McCarthy will step in and take over for the Vikings, which would be bad news for the fantasy value of Justin Jefferson, Aaron Jones Sr., and their entire offense on Sunday.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Carson Wentz set to start for Week 2
items.desc: Carson Wentz is set to be Minnesota's starting quarterback in their matchup against the Chicago Bears in Week 2.
items.impact: The Vikings have ruled out Kyler Murray (concussion) ahead of Sunday's game and announced that Wentz would be the starter in his absence. That's good news for the fantasy outlook of Justin Jefferson and Aaron Jones Sr. this week, as Minnesota's offense has been able to produce ample fantasy points in the few occasions that Wentz has been at the helm for the team.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jauan Jennings (personal) won't play Sunday
items.desc: Jauan Jennings (personal) won't play in Sunday's game against the Chicago Bears.
items.impact: The veteran wideout is going to be absent for Sunday's game. He is currently dealing with a personal issue of some kind, though the details of it are unknown at this point. Jordan Addison may see a little bit more work with Jennings out of the lineup.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Brian O'Neill (knee) questionable for Sunday
items.desc: Brian O'Neill (knee) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Chicago Bears.
items.impact: O'Neill will carry an injury designation heading into the weekend after missing practice earlier in the week due to some kind of a knee issue. If he is ruled out for Sunday's game, Minnesota's offensive line will be weaker than usual in a divisional matchup against the Bears.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Kyler Murray (concussion) ruled out for Sunday
items.desc: Kyler Murray (concussion) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Chicago Bears.
items.impact: Murray was progressing well through the NFL's concussion protocols this week, but he will ultimately have to end up missing a game due to the big hit that he suffered in Week 1. It looks likely that he will be back in time for Week 3, but Carson Wentz is expected to serve as Minnesota's starter in the meantime, which is good news for the fantasy value of Justin Jefferson in a prime matchup against the Bears this week.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Tanner Ingle signs with Rams' active roster
items.desc: The Rams signed S Tanner Ingle from the practice squad to the active roster.
items.impact: Ingle will add depth in the secondary for the Rams with Kam Kinchens battling a hamstring injury.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Juwan Johnson (illness) off injury report Week 2
items.desc: Juwan Johnson is off the injury report for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
items.impact: Johnson was a late addition to the injury report this week with an illness. He'll be on the TE1/TE2 radar for fantasy managers this week.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Cameron Jordan (hamstring) off injury report Week 2
items.desc: Cameron Jordan is off the injury report for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
items.impact: Jordan returned to a full practice on Friday. He'll be a full-go on Sunday against Baltimore.
